answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may bid for paid work, then slash that stake when independent audits show fabricated activity or collusive claims. Splitting one actor into many identities does not multiply influence for free: every identity ties up more capital, while repeated violations destroy it. Audits can sample work across a mesa of tasks; pigment labels may help track provenance, but the zenith of the defense is the attacker’s rising, measurable cost per credible identity.
